Diagnosis:
The failing test `testIterateDOM` calls a helper `doTestIterate` with the model `DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM`. This helper creates a `JXPathContext` with a namespace prefix "a" mapped to "ns", and then asserts that iterating pointers by the XPath "/a:doc/a:elem" returns two distinct pointers ("/a:doc[1]/a:elem[1]" and "/a:doc[1]/a:elem[2]"). The bug report describes a problem when multiple prefixes are mapped to the same namespace URI "ns": iterating pointers returns the first element twice, missing the second one with a different prefix.

The key method is `JXPathContext.iteratePointers(String)`, which calls `JXPathContextReferenceImpl.iteratePointers(String)`, which compiles the expression and calls `Expression.iteratePointers(EvalContext)`. This method calls `Expression.compute(EvalContext)` (abstract) and then tries to turn the result into pointers.

The issue is likely caused by the namespace resolving when multiple prefixes point to the same namespace URI, causing the XPath evaluation to incorrectly match the same element twice but skip the other with a different prefix. The recent reports mention regressions around `NamespaceResolver` and how prefix-to-namespace mappings are stored and used, which is relevant.

In summary, the bug results because the internal namespace resolver or namespace mapping caching incorrectly handles multiple prefixes mapped to the same URI, causing duplicates and missed elements during iteration by XPath with namespaces.

The fix will likely involve the namespace resolver implementation, ensuring it correctly differentiates elements by prefix and properly handles multiple prefixes for the same namespace URI when resolving XPath expressions and iterating pointers.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
